title: Best clarinet players and old Tio
summary: French names Andy, Alfred and old Tio as best clarinetists; the interviewer discusses Tio's records and reading.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Yeah, but he came back. He was married to Bricktop, you know. I was going to ask you some of your favorite musicians were through the years. Who was some of the best clarinet players you've heard?
Well the best I ever heard Ron Yarlene was uh... Andy? Andy and T.O.
That's a young T.O.?
Oh no, the old T.O.
The daddy, not the son.
The old man.
What was he good for? Was he a jazz man or a reading man? He's a good reader but he played on them film.
He played a...what you call them high clannets? Not the... E-flat.
Well, Alfred too, good clannets as well. Yeah. Plenty good clannets played on him.
Oh, he could get that clannets. Yeah. Yeah. Over all...he could all of them.
Yeah. Well, I could take a e-plate, clannets and plates and you'll see many of them do that.
T.O. had one. Yeah.
Yeah, T.O. had one. Yeah, T.O. had one. Yeah, come on. We had plenty of them down there, clannets played. Yeah, that was good.
Who did T.O. work with?

 But I know he always played with P.R. when I know him.

He did. They went to New York, maybe they didn't? That time they went to New York.

But he didn't get a chance to really get off on them too good. Sometimes you can hear him good, but not often. Usually, you know, he's just reading, and you can't hear what he can do. Let's see. Did you ever make any records, you sir?
